name: Salesforce Certified JavaScript Developer
delivery: Booked through Trailhead Academy and delivered by Pearson VUE, either online proctored (OnVUE) or at a testing center. No hard-copy or online materials allowed during the exam.
maintenance: Complete the JavaScript Developer certification maintenance badge on Trailhead once a year (Summer '26 badge due August 2027); the credential expires if you miss the deadline.

sections.title: Variables, Types, and Collections
objectives: Given a scenario, write code to create variables and initialize them correctly.
Given a business requirement, utilize strings, numbers, and dates effectively.
Given a scenario or example, demonstrate awareness of type coercion and its effects.
Given a specific scenario, distinguish truthy or falsey evaluations.
Given a list of data, demonstrate data manipulation with arrays.
Given a JSON response, demonstrate how to operate the JSON object.

sections.title: Objects, Functions, and Classes
objectives: Given a business requirement, locate the best function implementation.
Given a business requirement, apply fundamentals of object implementation to solve the business requirement.
Given a business requirement, apply fundamentals of class implementation to solve the business requirement.
Given a JavaScript module, give examples of how to use the module.
Given a block of code, analyze the variable scope and the execution flow.

sections.title: Browser and Events
objectives: Given a business requirement, utilize Events, event handlers, and propagation.
Given a business requirement, evaluate and manipulate the DOM.
Given a scenario, utilize the Browser Dev Tools to investigate code behavior.
Given a scenario and requirements, utilize browser specific APIs.

sections.title: Debugging and Error Handling
objectives: Given a scenario, handle errors properly.
Given code to be debugged, use the console and breakpoints.

sections.title: Asynchronous Programming
objectives: Given a scenario, apply asynchronous programming concepts.
Given a scenario, use event loop and event monitor or determine loop outcomes.

sections.title: Server Side JavaScript
objectives: Given a scenario and requirements, infer which Node.js implementation is a good solution.
Given a scenario and requirements, infer which Node.js CLI command is a good solution.
Know the core Node.js modules and given requirements, infer which Node.js library/framework is a good solution.
Given a scenario and requirements, distinguish which Node.Js Package Management solution is the most fitting.

sections.title: Testing
objectives: With a block of code and the associated Unit Test, determine where the test is ineffective and modify it to make it more effective.

tips: Read the official exam guide first and weight study time by section: Objects, Functions, and Classes (25%) and Variables, Types, and Collections (23%) are almost half the exam.
Do the three official Cert Prep modules on Trailhead; each has practice scenarios and flashcards for its sections.
Run code, don't just read it: a browser console or `node` in a terminal answers most 'what does this print?' questions in seconds.
Expect short code snippets that ask what gets logged, which line throws, or which options are correct; trace them line by line on paper.
Multiple-select questions tell you how many answers to choose; all must be correct to score.
There is no penalty for guessing, so answer every question and flag uncertain ones for review.
Budget under 2 minutes per question (up to 65 questions in 105 minutes) and leave 10 minutes to revisit flagged items.
Up to 5 unscored questions are mixed in; don't let an odd question rattle you.
Know the classic traps cold: == vs === coercion, typeof null, hoisting and the temporal dead zone, `this` in arrow functions, and microtasks before timers.
Questions align to the Summer '22 release (mid-2022 JavaScript); features added to JavaScript, Node.js or Jest since then won't be needed.
For online proctoring, run the Pearson VUE system test in advance, clear your desk, and check in early with a valid government-issued ID.
Schedule the exam date first; a fixed deadline keeps a 4-6 week plan on track.

studyPlan.focus: Browser and Events + Debugging and Error Handling

notes: Name: the exam guide and credential page call it 'Salesforce Certified JavaScript Developer'; 'JavaScript Developer I' survives in URLs and in the Trailhead trail and Cert Prep titles. The credential page links a Trailhead Academy exam page whose URL ends in 'JS-Dev-101', which suggests the exam code, but that page wasn't reachable from here and the guide shows no code, so the code is left out.

Second requirement: older materials describe the credential as the exam plus the Lightning Web Components Specialist superbadge. The current guide (read 2026-11-17) lists 'Prerequisite: None' and no other requirement, and the recommended trailmix lists only the multiple-choice exam task. This file treats the exam as the only requirement.

Release: the guide says questions align to the Summer '22 release (mid-2022), so the JavaScript is roughly ECMAScript 2022 and the Node.js of that time (18 current, 16 LTS). Features finished later are newer than the exam: change-array-by-copy (toSorted, toReversed, toSpliced, with) and findLast/findLastIndex (ES2023), Object.groupBy/Map.groupBy and Promise.withResolvers (ES2024), new Set methods, iterator helpers and Promise.try (ES2025), and later. ES2022 itself (at(), Object.hasOwn, error cause, class fields with private # and static blocks, top-level await) was brand new at that release. Teach these as 'newer' and never make them the only right answer.

Node.js versions: current docs show features newer than the exam: the --watch flag (added v18.11), the test runner (--test, stable in v20), --env-file (v20.6), require() of ES modules (v22/v20.17) and fetch as stable (v21; unflagged experimental since v18.0). The current docs also mark process.nextTick() as 'Legacy: use queueMicrotask() instead'; the exam era treated nextTick as a normal API. Avoid questions that depend on these.

Jest: Jest 30 removed the alias matchers (toBeCalled, toBeCalledWith, lastCalledWith, toReturn and others). The exam era used Jest 28, where they still worked. Teach the full names (toHaveBeenCalled, toHaveBeenCalledWith…) and mention the old aliases only as old names.
Exam guide spelling: objectives say 'falsey' and 'Node.Js'; they are copied verbatim here. Lessons use 'falsy' (MDN's spelling).

Weights: the guide gives 23/25/17/7/13/8/7, and the Cert Prep 'Get Started' unit lists the same numbers. The Cert Prep unit calls the sections 'Browsers and events' and 'Server-side JavaScript'; the guide's names ('Browser and Events', 'Server Side JavaScript') are used here.

Testing has a single objective (find where a unit test is ineffective and improve it). The Cert Prep unit adds unit vs integration vs end-to-end tests, black-box vs white-box, false positives and negatives, console.assert and Jest as the tool; the lessons cover those.

Maintenance: the guide says once a year; the Trailhead Certification Release Maintenance Schedule (read 2026-11-17) lists the JavaScript Developer maintenance badge as a Summer cycle badge: available August 2026, due August 2027.
Unscored items: the guide says 'up to five'; 5 is the maximum, not a guaranteed count.

Delivery: Trailhead Academy booking and Pearson VUE delivery (OnVUE online or a testing center) are confirmed by the Trailhead help article 'Scheduling an Exam'; the guide itself only says 'onsite at a testing center or in an online environment'.

Reading the references: developer.mozilla.org, tc39.es, jestjs.io and docs.npmjs.com were blocked from this environment. Their official source repositories (mdn/content, tc39/proposals, jestjs/jest docs, npm/cli docs) were read instead on 2026-11-17; the outline cites the public URLs.
Pricing in currencies other than USD and JPY was not checked.

boss.name: The Coercion Sphinx
boss.taunt: Is [] truthy? Does '1' + 1 make 2? Answer, or be coerced!
boss.defeat: Strict equality… no tricks… you see clearly.

boss.name: The Closure Hydra
boss.taunt: Cut off a head and my inner functions still remember it!
boss.defeat: Lexical scope… you saw it coming…

boss.name: The Event Kraken
boss.taunt: One click, and it bubbles to every handler I've got! Blub!
boss.defeat: One listener… on the parent… delegated… blub.

boss.name: The Stack Trace Toad
boss.taunt: Uncaught TypeError! Find the line if you can! Ribbit!

boss.name: The Callback Hydra
boss.taunt: A callback in a callback in a callback! Untangle my heads!
boss.defeat: async… await… one straight line… my heads fall.

boss.name: The Package Robot
boss.taunt: Caret or tilde? I'll install whatever version I like! BEEP!

boss.name: The False-Positive Frog
boss.taunt: My test is green and it checks nothing at all! Ribbit!
boss.defeat: Real asserts… and you awaited… croak.
